Governor Bullock's argument for hiking into a supply shock rests on second-round effects from higher-for-longer oil, and she made it on Monday into a crude market that has since broken 90 and a domestic economy that has since started shedding jobs. The honest counterweight, and it is the reason AUD is +1 rather than 0, is that the same survey showed output price inflation strengthening - businesses passing costs on is her thesis, not against it - and the cash rate at 4.35% is still the highest policy rate on this board. catalysts.note: 01:30Z, Employment Change at +22.5K consensus after a -15.8K contraction, with the unemployment rate forecast unchanged at 4.5%. The most asymmetric event on this page. catalysts.note: 07:30Z with 0.00% carried as both consensus and TEForecast by TradingEconomics, 0.00% against 0.00% previous on the ForexFactory calendar, and a Reuters poll in which every economist expects a hold, a majority through 2027. catalysts.note: 08:00Z, a separate red folder 30 minutes after the assessment, and the part that usually moves the franc more than the rate line. An explicit threat to counter appreciation is read as a floor under EUR/CHF and USD/CHF and takes CHF to -1; a raised conditional forecast with the intervention language softened takes it to +1. EUR/CHF at 0.93874 is the pair the June wording was aimed at, and it overlaps the euro-area flash PMI release directly.

catalysts.note: Dhingra 09:30Z, Breeden 13:30Z, Lombardelli 14:00Z - three MPC voices in five hours, the day after sterling was downgraded to 0 on the fiscal overshoot and with only the 3/9 hike vote holding the case up. catalysts.note: 05:00Z at 1.5% forecast from 1.6%. catalysts.note: 09:15Z and now the decisive sterling event of the week, because GBP came down to 0 today and the only leg still holding it there is the September 17 vote split of 3/9 to hike and 0/9 to cut. Bailey has to address an October 1 Ofgem cap rise of 4% to 1,723 pounds that is locked into the October CPI the MPC reads in November, a labour market producing a +27.8K claimant count and -26.1K payrolled employees, and now a fiscal position running 8.1bn above the OBR forecast five weeks before an October 28 Budget. If he frames the energy cap as something the MPC must act on, sterling goes back to +1; if he frames it as something to look through, the last leg goes and GBP heads for -1.

catalysts.note: Durable goods 12:30Z with the headline -0.3% forecast from +1.1% and core +0.6% from +0.4%, then revised UoM sentiment 14:00Z at 47.4 from 47.8 with revised inflation expectations against a 4.6% previous. Schmid speaks 13:20Z and Hammack 18:00Z.

catalysts.event: RBA Governor Bullock speaks - Reserve Bank of Australia
catalysts.note: HAPPENED at 03:10Z Monday, a CEDA fireside chat in Sydney with Q&A open to the media, seven days before the September 28-29 board meeting. The wire-reported lines were that supply shocks are difficult for monetary policy to deal with, that policy needs to deal with second-round effects on inflation, higher-for-longer oil prices, businesses more willing to pass on cost increases, a general consensus that the neutral rate has risen, and upside inflation risks materialising. The RBA published no transcript or prepared text for a chat streamed live only, so every line is wire-reported rather than verbatim from rba.gov.au. What has changed since she spoke is the entire factual basis: WTI has broken 90 to 89.263 and is -12.85% on the week, and S&P Global's September flash survey has put manufacturing at 49.3 from 52.0 with private firms cutting jobs for the first time since May. Market reaction on the day was four pips. AUD is downgraded to +1 today.

catalysts.event: Bundesbank President Nagel speaks - European Central Bank
catalysts.note: HAPPENED in London. Nagel said high energy prices had driven inflation off the 2026 target, that he is not concerned about the labour market, that rates are 'still in neutral territory' and that he cannot exclude the possibility the ECB needs to turn mildly restrictive. That is the first Governing Council member to put restrictive territory on the table out loud, and it points the same way as TradingEconomics' model path of 3.15% in 2027 and 2.65% in 2028. It is not a dated hike, which is the trigger this page set for a EUR upgrade, and the currency did not confirm it - EUR/USD fell 0.18% to 1.14273. Lagarde also spoke at 11:00Z. The October 8 Monetary Policy Meeting Accounts are the next scheduled read on whether the Council is actually discussing a further move.

catalysts.event: UK public sector net borrowing - Office for National Statistics
catalysts.note: HAPPENED at 06:00Z and it is the reason sterling is downgraded today, which is unusual for a low-impact release. Borrowing was 18.3 billion pounds in August against a 15.7 billion market expectation and 3.5 billion above the OBR profile, the second-highest August on record unadjusted. Borrowing in the financial year to August was 77.3 billion - 2.2 billion less than the same period last year but 8.1 billion above the OBR forecast - against a fiscal rule requiring the current budget in surplus or a deficit no wider than 0.5% of GDP by 2029/30, with the Budget dated October 28. Friday's upgrade to +1 named a fiscal-drag Budget as one of four invalidations; this is the first of those four to produce hard evidence.

catalysts.note: 04:30Z, and the biggest single disagreement between market pricing and the canonical source anywhere on this board. MNI called the hike nearly fully priced on September 21 and CBA has it near 90%; TradingEconomics carries 4.35% by the end of this quarter, which covers the meeting, and has never priced the move at all. The gap widened rather than narrowed today, because crude broke 90 and the September flash survey put manufacturing at 49.3 with firms cutting jobs - both of which undercut the second-round-effects doctrine the hike rests on - while output price inflation in the same survey strengthened, which supports it. Beyond the meeting the sell side is split: CBA at 4.60% then cuts from August 2027 against UBS at a 4.85% terminal. Thursday's labour force survey is the last input.

catalysts.note: 23:50Z and the nearest scheduled insight into a 7-2 vote in which Asada and Sato dissented AGAINST the move to 1.25%. A Summary that dates the next move takes JPY to +1. It arrives after a week in which the Bank reportedly ran a rate check with market participants and the Ministry of Finance had three shut Tokyo sessions to work in.

catalysts.note: The next scheduled read on the Governing Council's thinking, and now materially more interesting than it was: TradingEconomics carries no dated ECB decision row at all after September 10, its model path is 3.15% in 2027, and Nagel has just said publicly that rates are 'still in neutral territory' and that mildly restrictive policy cannot be excluded. If the accounts show the Council actually discussing a further hike, that is the trigger this page has set for taking EUR to +1. Schnabel has separately argued rates may need to rise further.

Core inflation rising to 2.4% from 2.3% is the one Canadian data point pointing at pass-through. A survey showing firms expecting to pass energy costs on takes CAD back toward 0 even at 89 dollar crude.

catalysts.note: Three events on one date and they interact. FOMC Minutes from September land October 7.

catalysts.event: UN General Assembly, Hormuz status and the Saudi East-West pipeline restart
catalysts.note: The single concentrated risk to this entire page and it is not diversified. geopolitics: The transmission is still running in the de-escalation direction and the price has now broken a round number on it, but the news underneath became genuinely contradictory in the last 24 hours and that contradiction is the tradeable part. Start with what is not in dispute. WTI is 89.263, down 1.39% on the day and 12.85% on the week across five consecutive losing sessions, and Brent has gone under 100 at 98.412 and -7.01%. Gas has followed: EU gas 71.28 and -8.65% on the week, German gas 74.11 and -7.98% on the day for -11.32% on the month, UK gas 177.50 and -8.25%. The physical repair is real and advancing - Saudi Arabia is preparing to restart its East-West pipeline, damaged by drone attacks earlier this month, with exports potentially resuming this week, CENTCOM has supported more than a billion barrels leaving the Gulf and over 2,000 assisted commercial transits, and its commander says the primary transit lanes are clear of mines after US Navy underwater drones identified more than a hundred suspected devices. Now the contradiction. Kyodo News and Reuters, each citing Iranian officials, reported on September 22 that Tehran had proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and returning to talks if Washington eases its military pressure and begins lifting the blockade on Iranian ports, with the proposal said to have been approved by Mojtaba Khamenei and the Supreme National Security Council and transmitted through intermediaries. That report is what took Brent below 100. Within hours the semi-official Fars news agency denied it, citing sources close to Iran's negotiating team, called the reports unreliable and inaccurate, and said explicitly that they were designed to lower oil prices; an Iranian military source told Fars the strait will remain closed as long as hostile actions by the United States continue. Layered on top, Trump used his General Assembly address to say he has 'a big decision to make' between a deal that lets Iran rebuild and annihilating the Islamic Republic 'and do it quickly', and predicted that any deal would not come until after the November midterm elections - 'I believe we'll make a deal right after the election'. Rubio says Trump is open to meeting Pezeshkian, who addresses the chamber today, but no meeting is scheduled. So the diplomatic timeline was pushed out by two months and the Iranian side publicly repudiated the story that moved the price, and crude fell anyway. The honest conclusion is that the market is trading the physical repair rather than the diplomacy, which is defensible - barrels are moving and a pipeline is restarting - but it means the price has stopped discounting the political tail at all. The FX read has five legs. First, Canada: the terms-of-trade support is gone and both benchmarks are now through the level Macklem's conditional was written at, since he said inflation would be expected to edge up 'if oil prices stay near US$100 per barrel' and that the Bank will not let energy effects broaden into persistent inflation. CAD holds -1 and USD/CAD at 1.40818 is the widest gap on this page - though core inflation rising to 2.4% and a TE path with no cut before 2028 are why it is not -2. Second, Australia, and this is the leg that moved today: Bullock's case for hiking into a supply shock rests on second-round effects from higher-for-longer oil, and crude has now broken 90 while S&P Global's September flash survey put manufacturing at 49.3 from 52.0 with private firms cutting jobs for the first time since May. AUD comes down to +1 and the near fully priced September 29 hike is the most asymmetric position on this board. Third, the havens, which have simply stopped working: gold is 4342.95 and could not hold gains with Middle East headlines live, because a 4.97% US 10-year and a dollar at new highs are doing the pricing, while the franc has weakened 2.38% against the dollar on the month through a shooting war - which also removes the pressure the SNB wrote its intervention language for, one day before it has to repeat or revise it. Fourth, equities: falling Brent, German gas down 11.32% on the month and a Bund at 3.4538% are why the DAX closed flat at 25,579 on Tuesday and trades 25,715 now, roughly 3.4% below its record, straight through the worst CDU state result in postwar German history. The new headwind there is monetary rather than political, because Nagel has just put restrictive ECB policy on the table. Fifth, the metals split: copper at 6.7455 and +4.88% on the week near its record is a physical supply story that has nothing to do with the war, and it is the only commodity leg still supporting a currency on this board. The risk to all five is one risk rather than five. Short crude is now the crowded side after a 12.85% week, the Iranian denial is on the record, the Saudi pipeline is still damaged, Trump has put annihilation and a post-midterm timeline in the same speech, and Pezeshkian speaks today.
